title: Amortized decrease-key complexity of standard pairing heaps
formal: Determine, up to constant factors, the amortized decrease-key bound \(d(N)\) of the standard two-pass pairing heap, while insert, meld and find-min are charged \(O(1)\) and delete-min is charged \(O(\log(2+N))\). The bound is required for every finite sequence starting from empty heaps with at most \(N\) live items in all heaps combined.
definitions: A heap is a rooted heap-ordered tree. Link compares two roots and makes the larger root the new leftmost child of the smaller. Insert links a singleton to the root; meld links the two roots. Decrease-key receives a handle, reduces its key and, if it is not a root, cuts its whole subtree and links it to the root. Delete-min removes the root, links consecutive children from left to right in disjoint pairs, leaving an unpaired last child unchanged, then combines the resulting roots from right to left by successive links. Find-min reads the root. Keys are opaque ordered values; ties follow a fixed identity order. Constant-size nodes have enough sibling and parent pointers for a cut in constant time. Charge comparisons, links, cuts and pointer work. An admissible upper bound is a function \(d\ge1\) for which a universal \(C\) bounds total cost by \(C(a+b\log(2+N)+c d(N))\), where \(a\) counts the constant-cost operations, \(b\) delete-min operations and \(c\) decreases. A tight answer must also prove that every admissible charge function dominates the supplied rate within a universal constant for sufficiently large \(N\); the constants cannot depend on the sequence. Variants changing either pass, rank metadata or the linking discipline are different algorithms.
why: A tight analysis would resolve the central complexity uncertainty for one of the simplest and most widely studied self-adjusting priority queues.

context_blocks.text: A logarithmic-logarithmic lower bound rules out the original constant-amortized decrease-key expectation under the other standard charges. Related self-adjusting heaps attaining that bound do not automatically analyze the original two-pass algorithm.

The July 2026 paper proves a smaller gap for pure pairing heaps and announces an improved bound for standard pairing heaps in a forthcoming companion paper. Its conclusion explicitly retains the remaining gap. The announcement is recorded separately from a checked proof for the standard algorithm.

progress.text: The classical lower bound is \(\Omega(\log\log N)\) under the usual other-operation charges.

The pure variant has \(O(\log\log N\log\log\log N)\) decrease-key. The conclusion announces \(O((\log\log N)^2\log\log\log N)\) for standard pairing heaps in forthcoming work; no independent verification of that announced proof was performed.

answer_criterion: Supply a growth rate with a complete Lean-checked upper analysis and matching lower bound under the charge convention defined here. An improved upper bound without tightness, or a tight bound for another heap variant, is insufficient.

sentences: The standard pairing heap uses a fixed two-pass consolidation during delete-min.
Its pointer operations are simple, but decreases can affect the cost of future consolidations.
The target is a tight amortized charge for decrease-key with the conventional costs for other operations.
A logarithmic-logarithmic lower bound is known.
Results for pure, multipass, smooth or rank-pairing heaps concern different algorithms.
